title: From Aus Minimum Wage 2025 to Your Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week formula. Includes aus minimum wage 2025 context, tax, super, and state differences in ordinary-time earnings.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay if I work casual hours?
faqs.a: If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. When using the timesheet, type your base hourly rate (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The annual estimate then uses the loaded rate × hours per week × 52. Remember that casual loading is paid in lieu of leave entitlements, and super is still paid on top of the loaded rate.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. As of 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for full-time adults. Award rates are industry- or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Commission and are often higher. Your pay must meet whichever minimum applies to you. The aus minimum wage 2025 was lower; check the Fair Work Ombudsman for historical rates.

faqs.q: How does superannuation affect my total remuneration?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee contributions are 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, above which the employer does not have to pay super on the excess.

bodyMarkdown:
## Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

To estimate your annual gross pay from an hourly rate, multiply your rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role based on 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives a quick benchmark. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure. For example, a 20-hour part-time week would use 20 instead of 38. The result is a gross figure before tax and other deductions. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards. Many awards and agreements use it as the base for ordinary hours. When you use [the timesheet](/), you can enter any weekly hours, but 38 is the default for full-time calculations.

### Fortnightly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly gross by 2. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly gross is $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you match your pay cycle.

## Understanding the Aus Minimum Wage 2025

The aus minimum wage 2025 was the rate set by the Fair Work Commission for that financial year. It increased on 1 July 2025 and again on 1 July 2026. As of 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for full-time adults, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. If you are comparing your pay to the aus minimum wage 2025, note that the 2025 rate was lower; the Fair Work Commission publishes historical rates on its website.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

Many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum than the National Minimum Wage. Award rates vary by industry and occupation. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate than the national minimum. Always check your applicable award via [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman. The National Minimum Wage applies only if no other instrument covers you.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are paid a loading (usually 25%) instead of paid leave entitlements. When using [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate (the rate before loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator will add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The annual estimate then uses the loaded rate.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adults vary across Australian states and territories. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings survey (May 2026), the national average for full-time adult ordinary time is $2,083.70 per week. However, states like New South Wales and Western Australia tend to have higher averages due to industry mix (e.g., mining, finance), while Tasmania and South Australia often sit below the national figure. These differences reflect variations in industry composition, cost of living, and local labour markets. The ABS publishes state-level data; you can explore it via [reference tables](/data).

### Why State Averages Matter

If you are negotiating a salary or comparing job offers, knowing the average ordinary-time earnings in your state gives context. For example, a full-time role in mining in Western Australia may pay well above the national average, while a similar role in hospitality in Tasmania may pay closer to the minimum. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. Use [average pay](/topics/average-pay) resources to see broader trends.

## Tax and Super: What Comes Off and What Goes On

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

Tax is calculated on your annual gross pay using the progressive tax scale:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax-free threshold is assumed. If you have a HELP debt or are liable for the Medicare levy surcharge, your tax will be higher. This estimate does not include those. For a more precise calculation, use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tools.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830; earnings above that do not attract compulsory super. You can read more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Putting It All Together: An Example

Suppose you earn $35 per hour as a full-time permanent employee working 38 hours per week.
- Weekly gross: $35 × 38 = $1,330
- Fortnightly gross: $1,330 × 2 = $2,660
- Annual gross: $1,330 × 52 = $69,160
- Estimated tax (2026–27): approximately $11,717 (including Medicare)
- Estimated super (12%): $8,299.20 paid on top
- Annual take-home (after tax): about $57,443

If you were casual at the same base rate, your loaded rate would be $43.75 per hour ($35 × 1.25), giving a higher annual gross of $86,450, but without paid leave.

## Important Notes

This conversion is an estimate. It does not account for unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or irregular hours. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2027 thresholds were not confirmed here. Always consult a professional for your specific situation.

For more detailed breakdowns, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guides.
